content.comment_body: When I connect to the web server of [product_name] [version_no] Pure, I see a blank BM screen, although the menu and buttons respond to activation and deactivation (with colors indicating status). Everything else works fine. Is it normal to have a blank BM screen, or did I misconfigure something? Does the Pure version, since it has no physical display, emulate a screen through the microcontroller?

Through the web server, the system menu isn't shown and you cannot configure the system directly. The web server displays only the message texts you have set up, and the virtual buttons only affect your program if they are programmed as interactive keys. This behavior is the same for Pure versions.

If you'd like to use a message text with the web server in [product_name], each message text needs to be enabled for web display. Open the message text properties and you'll find options to select where the message shows: only [product_name] display, only TDE, only web server, or a combination. The web server itself must also be enabled in [product_name]. This can be done under Tool/Transfer/Access control; enable the web server and set a password, then apply the settings. Based on your choices, you'll see messages on the [product_name] display and/or in the web server.
Thanks to [user_name] and [user_name]! This is helpful, but I still can't access the device's local system screen on [product_name]. It seems that feature is not available.

I have [product_name] [version_no] with display. I've configured message texts for LOGO TD and allowed web server access. I'm able to connect to the system via my browser without issues. To make it work, you need to add a message to your system, enable both the display and web server options for it. If you need further help, you can contact me on Skype at [user_name].

Using the web server in [product_name] [version_no] doesn't require a physical display or TDE. Message texts are what show information on the web server. If you've enabled the web server and created message texts, but see an empty screen in one of the views, make sure the message text is enabled for the display. Go to message text properties and check the relevant options in LSC [version_no]. The attached example helps explain this. The web server works and shows messages with a [product_name] [version_no] Pure even without an additional TDE.

The web server works well—I can interact with keys and texts and display counters. However, I can't access the local system screen where I can start, stop, save, load programs, or change setup options for [product_name]. According to information from [user_name], this feature is not supported.

Hello, I'm not sure if you've solved the issue. It seems you've tried all recommended steps, but the web server still displays a blank screen. Please refer to the attachment for a solution to your problem.

The earlier suggestions are correct—the message text screen requires the web server option to be enabled. When viewing the web server, the display updates in real time based on the message text shown on [product_name]. As a side note, the manual also mentions that port 8080 should be open, which is already enabled by default and usually doesn't affect display setup.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have observed that the web server feature on [product_name] [version_no] Pure shows a blank BM screen instead of the local system menu, although message texts and program elements can be accessed and interacted with. The system menu and core operations like start/stop and program saving/loading aren't available through the web server, which causes confusion since users expect full remote functionality. The web server is designed primarily for user-programmed messages and interactive keys, while system functionalities are intentionally not accessible remotely.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the web server of [product_name] [version_no] Pure to fully emulate the local system screen, including system menu access for tasks such as program management and device control. They want to be able to see and interact with these core system features remotely.
